What is CMS Open Payments?


CMS Open Payments (the Sunshine Act transparency program) publishes payments and transfers of value from drug and device manufacturers to physicians, non-physician practitioners, and teaching hospitals. Data is released as large public files and also exposed through the official Open Payments datastore query API on openpaymentsdata.cms.gov.
If you only need filtered rows — for example consulting fees in one state, or payments tied to a specific manufacturer — you usually do not need to download the entire yearly CSV.
Resolve the dataset UUID for the program year and payment type (general, research, or ownership).

articles.author: WeekendAiProjects
articles.description:
A personal assistant is easy to demo and hard to trust. The demo ends when the assistant answers. Trust starts when it can change your real calendar, when the model is small enough to run on your own computer, and when it says "done", and you need to know whether that's true.
We built Atlas, a personal assistant for one person. It runs on your own computer: an open-weight model in Ollama, your calendar over CalDAV with an app password, your tasks in a Markdown file, a memory you can read and edit, a page on your phone carried by Tailscale, and a briefing sent to your lock screen at seven by web push. This is an exchange from its phone page, word for word:
You: Move my dentist appointment to Friday at 10.
Atlas: The proposed change is waiting for your yes. Would you like to move the dentist…
articles.title: A 9B assistant built from our specs went from 6 to 32 right answers out of 32. Most of the fixes were code, not prompts

articles.author: Fenju Fu
articles.description:
Today's GitHub Trending tells a clear story: AI agents have enough capability. What they're missing is a way for users to actually use them.
vercel-labs/agent-desktop sits at #1 with 3,791 stars today — a Rust CLI that gives AI agents desktop control. It's a genuinely impressive piece of engineering. But look past the star count and you'll see the gap: to use it, you need a Rust toolchain, environment configuration, CLI fluency, and permission debugging. For developers, that's Tuesday. For everyone else, it's a wall.
We hit the same wall ourselves. We built agent capabilities — skill calling, cross-session memory persistence, local execution — and then watched users stare at the interface asking: "Okay, but what do I do first?"

It's not just agent-desktop. Look at the other hot repos toda…
articles.title: The Last Mile of Agent Adoption: Why `vercel-labs/agent-desktop` Proves Onboarding Matters More Than Capability

Amblyotube: engineering a dichoptic vision gym


The Binance $6.3 billion heist dominates headlines — state‑level actors, compromised infrastructure, billions vanishing in minutes. It is a stark reminder that even decentralized systems have weak points. Millions of adults with amblyopia (lazy eye) face a quieter vulnerability: they are told the ‘critical period’ for treatment closed in childhood, left with compromised depth perception, eye strain, and reduced coordination that subtly sabotages daily tasks — driving, sports, reading, even pouring coffee.  
Amblyotube, developed by Seven Sports for the Meta Quest platform, challenges that dogma. The app exploits the Quest’s dual‑eyepiece architecture to deliver two independent visual streams simultaneously, turning any YouTube clip into a st…

articles.author: xiun xiao
articles.description:
Originally published on the QuickSilver Pro blog.
Gemini 4 Argon is Google's new flagship reasoning model. On QuickSilver Pro it costs $2.00 / $10.00 per million tokens, against $1.00 / $5.00 for Claude Opus 5.5. We wanted to know whether it can stand in for Opus in a coding agent, and what that costs.
We tested this on 2026-10-27. Both models ran in the same agent, OpenCode, on six small but real coding tasks, and we graded every run with tests the agent never saw. Short answer: both passed every hidden test in every run. Gemini 4 Argon was slower and more expensive on every task: 134 seconds and $0.142 per task on average, against 82 seconds and $0.094 for Opus.
Agent: OpenCode 1.19.4, non-interactive (opencode run --auto), with QuickSilver Pro added as an OpenAI-compatible provider. The…
articles.title: Gemini 4 Argon vs Claude Opus 5.5 for coding agents

If you are building a homework helper or a tutoring agent, the hard part of a physics question is rarely the arithmetic. It is the formula, the units and the steps a student can follow. Language models are good at explaining and still slip on numbers, so we gave our physics calculators a door that agents can call directly.
Since yesterday (3 November 2026) the UsePhysics MCP server is listed in the official MCP Registry as com.usephysics/physics-calculators. It is a remote server (Streamable HTTP), free, and it needs no key:
https://usephysics.com/api/mcp

Four read-only tools:



tool
what it returns




list_calculators
every calculator: id, formula, input keys with units and defaults, page URL


calculate
the results with units, the formula, the worked steps where the engine can derive …
articles.title: A physics MCP server that shows its working: 31 calculators, 34 CODATA constants, no key

articles.author: Ashish
articles.description:
AI가 만든 단백질에 워터마크를 심는다면, 우리는 그 구조를 어떻게 '읽을 것인가'


딥마인드가 SynthID Bio를 공개했습니다. AI가 생성한 단백질 서열에 워터마크를 심으면서도 생물학적 기능을 유지하는 개념 증명입니다. 저는 이 발표에서 두 가지가 흥미로웠습니다.
첫째, 서열 수준의 출처 표시 문제가 본격적으로 다뤄지기 시작했다는 점. 둘째, 그와 동시에 구조 수준의 이해는 여전히 사람의 몫이라는 점입니다. 워터마크가 "이 서열은 AI가 만들었다"를 알려줘도, 그 단백질이 실제로 어떤 포켓을 갖고 어떤 리간드와 상호작용하는지는 별개의 질문이니까요. 출처는 기계가 찍어줄 수 있어도, 구조적 판단은 아직 사람의 워크플로우에 남아 있습니다.
여기서 제가 최근 써본 도구를 하나 공유합니다. NexoPeek라는 Meta Quest용 VR 분자 실험실입니다. 솔직히 처음엔 마케팅 냄새가 날까 봐 조심스러웠는데, 직접 써보니 구조 데이터를 다루는 방식이 꽤 실용적이었습니다. 무엇보다 데이터 라우팅 계층이 흥미로웠습니다.
유전자 이름 하나로 RCSB PDB, UniProtKB, AlphaFold DB, SWISS-MODEL, PDBe를 검색하고, UniProt 유전자 동의어 해석과 모델 검증을 거쳐 구조가 인간 크기로 로드됩니다.
Mol* 프리셋 6종으로 카툰, 볼앤스틱, 스페이스필 CPK, 분자 표면, B-factor 히트맵, 튜브 트레이스를 한 번에 전환합니다.
로컬 .pdb, .cif, .mol2, .gro, .xyz, .dx, .xtc, .py 파일을 정전기장선 지도·커스텀 결합 정의·전자밀도 볼륨과 함께 불러옵니다.
AI 포켓 예측(PrankWeb / P2Rank 또는 내장 오프라인 엔진)이 약물 가능 부위를 표시하고, Foldseek 파이프라인이 상동 구조를 겹쳐 도메인 기능 보존을 확인시켜 줍니다.
시퀀스의 잔기 필을 누르면 구조 위에 3D 할로로 투영되고, 트리거로 두 원자를 집으면 옹스트롬 거리가 나옵니다. 리간드 인스펙터는 수소 결합 네트워크를 평가하고 PubChem에서 3D 리간드를 가져옵니다.
기술적으로 흥미로운 지점은 이겁니다. 워터마킹은 서열이라는 1차원 문자열에 출처 메타데이터를 심는 문제지만, 실제 검증은 3차원 접힘과 결합 부위에서 일어납니다. AI 생성 단백질이 늘어날수록, 구조 검증과 시각적 소통의 병목은 어디서 생길까요? 서열 워터마킹이 출처 문제를 풀어도, 구조 생물학자와 약물 탐색 연구자가 실제로 판단하는 과정은 여전히 수작업에 가깝습니다. VR이 그 병목을 줄이는 데 실제로 도움이 되는지, 아니면 데모용 그 이상은 아닌지 궁금합니다.
제품 페이지: https://www.meta.com/experiences/nexopeek/1453797551140347/
(교육 및 연구 시각화 소프트웨어이며, 의학적 조언·진단·치료가 아닙니다. 포켓 예측·정렬 기능은 검증된 파이프라인과 전문가 판단을 대체하지 않습니다. 저는 이 제품과 이해관계가 없으며, 순수하게 구조 시각화 워크플로우 관점에서 공유합니다.)

articles.description:
Most AI Research Agents Don’t Need More Intelligence. They Need Better Search Hygiene.
Ask an AI assistant about an API that changed this morning and you may get a beautifully written answer that is already wrong.
That is the uncomfortable part of using language models for research. The response can sound confident, include plausible details, and still be built on stale knowledge. Developers feel this most when they are checking release notes, comparing prices, investigating a new dependency, or trying to understand a fast-moving incident. The model is not necessarily bad at reasoning. It simply has not been given fresh evidence.
The obvious fix is to add web search. The less obvious lesson is that search access alone does not make an agent trustworthy.
A useful research agent needs a habi…
articles.title: Most AI Research Agents Don’t Need More Intelligence. They Need Better Search Hygiene.

业务需求文档（BRD）：研究内容工厂 · 客户试点项目






  
  
  0. 文档目的与范围


回答四个问题：为什么做、做什么、不做什么、怎样算做成。
本需求不是来自客户的一句话「我们想用 AI 自动分析市场」，而是经过业务访谈与现状调研后，对客户真实业务流程的翻译。依据方法论的原则：先弄清真实业务，再决定哪些问题用流程优化、制度调整或软件开发解决——本文档区分了这三类。
范围：首单试点（2-3 周，托管代跑形态）。多租户、客户私有数据接入、自动发布为明确出界项（见 §8）。
客户（一家面向个人投资者的教育/内容服务机构，下称「内容方」）在首次沟通中只说了三句话：
「我们的研究内容生产太慢了，跟不上市场节奏。」
「小编写的东西经常被读者挑数字错误，很伤品牌。」
「我们想用 AI，但又怕 AI 编数字、乱荐股出合规事故。」

articles.description:
This is part of my build-in-public series on running LLM workflows in n8n in production. Everything here is a failure I actually watched happen, not a hypothetical.
Two workflows wrote to the same customer record on the same night. One updated the plan from a billing webhook. The other updated the contact details from a form submission. Both executions said success. The record that came out was neither update: the plan change was there, the contact change was gone, and nothing in either log suggested anything had been lost.
The mistake was assuming that two workflows touching the same row at different times is the same as two workflows touching it in sequence. It is not. Each workflow read the record, changed its own field, and wrote the whole record back. The second write overwrote the fi…

articles.author: Geovanne Bertonha
articles.description:
Every time I opened a new Claude Code session, I spent the first few minutes explaining my work again. Who the customer is. What we decided last week. How the weekly update should look. The agent was good at the task. It just knew nothing about the context around it.
So I built Get Things Done, an open-source, local-first work memory for Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot. This post is about one design decision behind it: storing that memory as plain Markdown files instead of in a database.
Not model training. Not embeddings hidden behind an API. Memory here means reviewed context: notes about your projects, the people you work with, past decisions and the formats you deliver, written down somewhere your agent can read before it starts a task.
The whole workspace is a folder:
